notes: A card either uses vocabulary in these lists or it fails to load.

`condition_keys` and `value_keys` are what an `if` can ask and what an amount can be. `counters_on` reads a counter count off an object, so "if this has no +1/+1 counters on it" is a `cmp` against `{"const": 0}` and needs no new op.

`selector_keys` is what an effect's `objects` or a target spec's `selector` may contain. `static_filter_keys` is the much smaller set a *static ability* may read, because a static may only read printed characteristics -- do not mistake it for the whole selector language.
An ability's `text` must be the printed sentence it implements: the residual gate asks each ability which line it claims, and anything unclaimed means the card is only half implemented.
An instant or sorcery puts its effects in `spell_effects`; a permanent puts them in `abilities`.
A static ability's filter may only read printed characteristics.
`snapshot` is how a card reads a value after its target has left -- there is no general last-known-information system.
A mana ability may contain only `add_mana`, or one `choose_mode` whose modes each contain only `add_mana`.

The expectation is checked in a sandbox: player 0 at 40 life with a deep mana base, two creatures, and an opponent holding a creature, a flier, an artifact and an enchantment. The card under test is the only card in hand.
